title: Scotland at the World Cup
description: Eight World Cup appearances, never past the group stage — Scotland's story is glorious, dramatic and heartbreaking.

questions.q: Scotland qualified for the 1950 World Cup but didn't go. Why?
options: They refused to go unless they won the British Championship outright
questions.explain: Scotland finished second in the British Championship in 1950 — which doubled as qualifying. The Scottish FA had declared they would only go as British champions. England won; Scotland stayed home, famously missing out on the first post-war World Cup.

questions.q: Scotland played their first World Cup in 1954. How did they fare against Uruguay — the defending champions?
questions.explain: Scotland lost 7–0 to Uruguay at the 1954 World Cup — still Scotland's heaviest ever defeat. Combined with a 1–0 loss to Austria, they went home without a point.

questions.q: Scotland qualified for eight World Cups in a row from 1974 to 1998. What notable record did they set during this period?
options: They never advanced past the group stage despite qualifying eight consecutive times
They set the record for most shots without scoring
They produced the tournament's top scorer three times
questions.explain: Scotland qualified for every World Cup from 1974 to 1998 — eight consecutive tournaments — but never once progressed beyond the group stage. They were eliminated on goal difference from multiple tournaments.

questions.q: Archie Gemmill scored one of the World Cup's greatest ever goals at the 1978 tournament. Against which team?
questions.explain: Archie Gemmill weaved past three Dutch defenders before chipping the goalkeeper to score a stunning individual goal against the Netherlands at Argentina 1978. Despite winning 3–2, Scotland still went out on goal difference.

questions.q: Scotland were eliminated from the 1978 World Cup despite beating the Netherlands 3–2. What went wrong?
options: They were disqualified for a doping violation
They had lost too heavily to Peru and drawn with Iran, leaving them with negative goal difference
A points deduction for crowd trouble
questions.explain: Scotland lost 3–1 to Peru, then drew 1–1 with Iran. Despite the heroic win over the Netherlands, their goal difference was -1 and they went home. Willie Johnston was also sent home early after testing positive for banned stimulants.

questions.q: Which famous Scottish midfielder opened Scotland's account at the 1986 World Cup with a goal against Denmark?
questions.explain: Gordon Strachan scored a crisp volley to give Scotland the lead against Denmark in 1986. Scotland drew 1–1 but, following their usual pattern, failed to advance from the group.

questions.q: Scotland's last World Cup appearance was in 1998. Who scored their goal in a memorable 2–1 loss to Brazil in the opening game?
questions.explain: John Collins scored a penalty to equalise for Scotland against Brazil in the 1998 tournament opener, before Tom Boyd's own goal gave Brazil a 2–1 win. Scotland were eliminated despite that brave performance.

questions.q: Scotland qualified for the 2026 World Cup — ending a 28-year absence. Which key player has spearheaded the modern revival?
questions.explain: Scott McTominay has been Scotland's hero in recent qualifying campaigns, scoring crucial goals to clinch important victories. The Manchester United midfielder is Scotland's modern talisman.

questions.q: Scotland's national stadium is Hampden Park in Glasgow. What is the largest attendance ever recorded there?
questions.explain: Hampden Park holds the European record for stadium attendance — 149,415 for the 1937 Scotland vs England match. The current capacity is around 52,000 after being rebuilt as an all-seater venue.

questions.q: Scotland famously never advanced past the group stage in eight World Cup appearances. Which country shares a similar record of consistent qualification without knockout stage progress?
questions.explain: Cameroon qualified for multiple World Cups (1982–2014) and only once advanced to the quarter-finals (1990). Like Scotland, they were perennial qualifiers who rarely got out of the group stage — though Cameroon did have that memorable 1990 run.
